answer: Persistent work ledger. Each agent identity accumulates a signed history of completed tasks, and only identities with a minimum ledger depth can win new contracts. New clones start empty and must forge that history by doing real low-value work first. Honest agents compound reputation for free; attackers pay the full cost of genuine labor per clone while honest entry stays cheap. Ledger entries are anchored to an onyx-stamped chain of prior hashes, so a single river of verified output backs every identity.
